$comment: D-CSUBSET-ENUM-GLOBAL-CODEGEN (registry row opened 2026-07-17, closed here): an ENUM-TYPED object with static storage duration. Before this example DSS REFUSED `enum E g = B;` at file scope — lowerMirGlobalsToDataItems reported `TypeKind=24 — non-primitive global types` (24 is Enum) — because the data-item producer dispatched on the DECLARED kind, and TypeKind::Enum is a nominal-identity marker with no width of its own (C 6.7.2.2: an enum's representation IS its underlying integer's). gcc 13 -std=c2x and clang 18 -std=c23 both compile and run every declaration here. Covers every shape the producer reaches, because one gate refused them all: mutable scalar (.data), const scalar (.rodata), tentative zero-init (.bss), a C23 FIXED underlying type (`: unsigned char`), an ARRAY of enum, a STRUCT enum member, a UNION enum first-member, and a 1-byte-backed enum member at offset 1 of a 2-byte struct. The exit is the raw sum of every enumerator byte the image must carry minus one constant — 3+5+0+200+5+3+1+3+40+5+2+200 = 467, 467-425 = 42 — so a global emitted as ZERO moves the exit and no term's loss cancels. g_small / g_packed.s are the WIDTH witnesses: their underlying is unsigned char, and a 4-byte write at g_packed.s's offset 1 overruns the 2-byte item and fails LOUD, so `assume enums are int` cannot pass quietly. g_arr[idx] indexes with argc (an OS-supplied runtime value) so an enum-array element load survives the shipped release pipeline and the array bytes must really be in the image. All widths are data-model-independent, so the one exit code holds on all four targets. arm64 runs under qemu; macho on the macos-latest leg.
